name: pihole
summary: Network-level DNS filtering and blocking service for controlled local network environments.
why_it_matters: Pi-hole can be strategically useful for homelab and controlled-network scenarios, but it is not currently justified as an active cross-platform Vrooli integration.
when_to_use: A deployment explicitly needs local DNS-level filtering or sinkholing.
A scenario targets homelab or appliance-style environments with network control.
You need demonstrable ad or tracker blocking as part of a managed local stack.
example_scenarios: Controlled family or office network deployments

platform_support.notes: The software can run in containers, but practical usefulness depends heavily on host networking control and local DNS topology.

prerequisites: Administrative control over local network DNS settings
Clear deployment boundary for appliance-like use
implementation_notes: Document networking assumptions explicitly if this is ever promoted.
Avoid representing this as a general-purpose developer dependency.
Prefer blueprint status until a real managed-network scenario needs it.
operational_notes: Port conflicts and DNS routing are the main operational risks.
Restore and backup of DNS configuration must be deliberate.
Health checks should verify DNS resolution behavior, not just an admin UI.
risks: Host networking assumptions vary too much across OSes for casual support claims.
